s: The architectural structure of which of the following temples exemplifies the independent style of the Chalukya-Cholas, incorporating Pallava and early Chalukya influences?
x:
The Draksharama Bhimeswara Temple represents the mature architectural style developed under the Chalukya-Cholas. Its design combines features of Pallava architecture, such as elegant structural planning, with Early Chalukyan elements, resulting in a distinctive regional style. This fusion later influenced temple architecture across the Godavari region. The Brihadeeshwara Temple at Thanjavur is a masterpiece of Imperial Chola architecture and does not represent the independent Chalukya-Chola style. The Padmakshi Temple at Hanamkonda is associated primarily with the Kakatiyas and reflects Kakatiya architectural traditions rather than Chalukya-Chola architecture. Therefore, Draksharama Temple is the correct answer.
Exam Note:
• Draksharama – Chalukya-Chola style
• Brihadeeshwara – Imperial Chola style
• Padmakshi – Kakatiya architecture

The Raichur Doab (Antarvedi) is the fertile tract of land situated between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers. Because of its fertile black cotton soil and strategic location, the Raichur Doab became one of the most disputed regions in medieval South India. It witnessed repeated conflicts among the Chalukyas, Cholas, Bahmanis, Vijayanagara rulers and the Deccan Sultanates. s: Who among the following dynasties founded the Kingdom of Berar?
x:
The Imad Shahi dynasty was one of the five Deccan Sultanates that emerged after the decline of the Bahmani Sultanate. It was founded by Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk in 1490 CE, with Ellichpur (Achalpur) as its capital. After the Bahmani kingdom weakened due to internal conflicts and provincial revolts, several governors declared independence. The five successor states were:
• Ahmadnagar – Nizam Shahis
• Bijapur – Adil Shahis
• Berar – Imad Shahis
• Bidar – Barid Shahis
• Golconda – Qutb Shahis The Kingdom of Berar remained independent until it was annexed by the Nizam Shahis of Ahmadnagar in 1574. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:

• Capital – Ellichpur (Achalpur)

Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
x: Vijnaneshwara was a prominent jurist in India during the first millennium CE. His treatise, the Mitakshara, dealt with inheritance, and is one of the most influential legal treatises in Hindu law. • Hemadri was a medieval scholar and jurist known for works on Dharmashastra and Ayurveda (specifically the Āyurveda Rasāyan commentary), as well as the encyclopedic Chaturvarga Chintāmaṇi. He was a 13th-century minister for the Yadava dynasty in Devagiri, Maharashtra, and is credited with developing the Hemadpanti temple architecture style. • Rajashekhara was an eminent Sanskrit poet, dramatist and critic. He was court poet of the Gurjara Pratiharas. He wrote Kavyamimamsa between 880 and 920 CE. The work is essentially a practical guide for poets that explains the elements and composition of a good poem. The fame of Rajashekhara rests firmly on his play Karpuramanjari, written in Sauraseni Prakrit. • Jimutavahana was a famous jurist from Bengal and the author of the Dayabhaga, an influential text on Hindu law.
